movement_source: row 'Cash net profit after tax ($M) continuing operations', column Full Year Ended 30 Jun 25 -> column Full Year Ended 30 Jun 26
headline: CBA's cash NPAT (continuing operations) rose $730 million or 7% to $10,982 million in FY26 vs FY25 ($10,252 million). Statutory NPAT rose $778 million or 8% to $10,911 million, with non-cash items narrowing from $(119)m (FY25) to $(71)m (FY26). Total operating income grew 6% (+$1,759m) to $30,224m; underlying operating expenses grew 6% (+$719m) to $13,585m; restructuring/notable items were $170m (vs $130m, +$40m); loan impairment expense rose $62m to $788m; corporate tax expense rose $208m to $4,699m. Operating performance (pre-provision profit) increased $1,000 million or 6% to $16,469 million.

drivers.narrative: NII increased $1,563 million or 7% to $25,586 million, driven by an $92 billion (8%) increase in average interest earning assets to $1,246 billion, partly offset by a 3 basis point decrease in NIM to 2.05%. Excluding liquids, underlying NIM was stable.

Other operating income increased $196 million or 4% to $4,638 million, driven by higher commissions (+$135m to $2,234m including CommInsure milestone payment), lending fees (+$12m to $924m), funds management (+$12m to $134m), and other income (+$46m to $156m including Gemini IPO gain), partly offset by lower trading income (−$9m to $1,190m).

Underlying operating expenses increased $719 million or 6% to $13,585 million. Staff expenses rose $288 million (4%) to $8,258m due to wage inflation and investment in technology/retail lenders/operations. IT services expenses rose $393 million (16%) to $2,782m from cloud computing, software licensing, and AI infrastructure. Occupancy decreased $19m (2%) to $938m. Other expenses increased $57m (4%) to $1,607m mainly from marketing.

Restructuring and notable items were $170 million in FY26 versus $130 million in FY25, an increase of $40 million. FY26 relates to provisions for NZ legal proceedings settlement, additional goodwill payment from ASIC's Better Banking review, and domestic customer remediation. FY25 related to domestic and NZ customer remediation and Bankwest restructuring provision.

Loan impairment expense increased $62 million or 9% to $788 million. Retail Banking Services increased $106m to $378m (geopolitical risk, cost-of-living pressures). New Zealand increased $11m to $66m (unemployment outlook deterioration). Business Banking decreased $45m to $310m (lower individual provisions, offset by higher collective). IB&M decreased $16m to $33m.

Corporate tax expense increased $208 million or 5% to $4,699 million, reflecting a 30.0% effective tax rate (down 50 bpts from 30.5%), primarily due to a decrease in non-deductible expenses. The higher tax reduced cash NPAT by $208m.

notable_items: FY26 notable items ($170m): NZ legal proceedings settlement, ASIC Better Banking goodwill payment, domestic customer remediation
FY25 notable items ($130m): domestic and NZ customer remediation, Bankwest restructuring provision
Non-cash items narrowing from $(119)m (FY25) to $(71)m (FY26), contributing $48m to the statutory-vs-cash convergence

disagreements.preferred: Both movements reported separately; cash is the primary measure
disagreements.explanation: The task asks for cash earnings movement. Statutory differs by $48m in non-cash items year-on-year (FY25: $(119)m, FY26: $(71)m). Both are reported and shown in evidence.

limitations: No walk/bridge waterfall chart was found that explicitly decomposes the $730m cash NPAT movement into component bars. All driver contributions are computed deltas from period columns (FY26 minus FY25) rather than bank-stated bridge bars, capping confidence at 80 for arithmetic-derived figures.

The bank states the drivers narratively ('driven by a 6% increase in operating income and a 6% increase in operating expenses, as well as a $62 million increase in loan impairment expense') but does not provide a formal bridge table summing to $730m.
Tax contribution is derived from the stated tax expense delta ($208m) rather than a bridge bar.
Research stopped early: the tool-call budget (40 calls) was reached, so the evidence behind this answer is less complete than a full run's.
Expenses are claimed on the underlying/notable split; the bank equally publishes the combined headline framing, so both claims are capped at 80.

Cash net profit after tax (cash NPAT or cash profit) from continuing operations increased $730 million or 7% on the prior year to $10,982 million. The result was driven by a 6% increase in operating income and a 6% increase in operating expenses 2, as well as a $62 million increase in loan impairment expense.
